Wattloft.subject: feat(plant-view): add passkey login as a Vault WebAuthn factor
Wattloft.line: Plant view is on the public internet, so a secret URL is not access control. v1 authenticates the one Operator with a password Wattloft stores, and optionally a passkey. Google, Apple, and Cognito are deferred: they are an identity product for one human, not a cheaper login.

form..subject: feat(plant-view): add passkey login as a Vault WebAuthn factor
form..line: The passkey is not an IdP. It is a WebAuthn credential (credential id + public key) injected as `OPERATOR_PASSKEY_CREDENTIAL` from Vault, the same env file as `OPERATOR_PASSWORD`. `POST /login` remains the password form. `POST /login/passkey` verifies an assertion against that public key and sets the same session cookie. There is no Plant view settings page to register a passkey.

optimisation:.subject: chore(agents): vendor Matt Pocock skills and lockfile
optimisation:.line: **Progressive disclosure** is the move down the ladder (out of the main file and behind a pointer) so the top stays legible. Not primarily a token optimisation: it is how the hierarchy is protected. Branching is the cleanest disclosure test: inline what every branch needs, and push behind a pointer what only some branches reach. When a document has steps, in-file reference that should be disclosed buries them and turns attending to them into a coin-flip: a variance lever, not just a legibility one.
